# CKTool JS Core Package

This package is part of the CKTool JS JavaScript client library suite
and is used to support other CKTool JS packages.

Don't use this package on its own. It is automatically pulled
in when you include `@apple/cktool.database`
in your `package.json` dependencies.

## Getting Started

See [Apple Developer Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cktooljs)
for more details on how to get started using CKTool JS.

## Strict Numeric Types

There are several branded types used to mark validated values.
For example, the `Int32` type is a branded numeric type that is 
assignaable to `number` but `number` is not directly assignable to it.

```ts
const a: number = toInt32(12); // OK
const b: Int32 = 12; // Error
```

## Casting Functions

This client library attempts to be as type-safe as possible.
There are several data types that must be validated in order to be
passed to an operation. For example, where an `Int32` would be expected,
you must first pass your constant through the `toInt32` cast function.
The `Int32` cast function does the following:
- Validates that the value is a numeric type.
- Validates that the number is an integer in `Int32` range.
- Returns an `Int32` value that will pass type checking.

Do NOT use type assertions to cast a related type, such as `number`
to a branded type. Such an approach is not guaranteed to compile in
future and an invalid value may be type asserted, which can lead
to errors down the line.

## Int64, Float, and Double Support

Support for `Int64`, `Float`, and `Double` is achieved with the [bignumber.js](https://github.com/MikeMcl/bignumber.js)
library. Whenever one of those numeric types are returned from an operation, it will be a
`BigNumber` instance. In order to perform operations on those instances, such
as addition or subtraction, you'll need to use the `BigNumber` methods.
See the documentation for `BigNumber` at https://github.com/MikeMcl/bignumber.js.

The `toInt64` cast function will do the following:
- Validates that the value is a numeric type.
- Validates that the number is an integer in `Int64` range.
- Returns a `BigNumber` instance of type `Int64`.

The `toFloat` cast function will do the following:
- Validates that the value is a numeric type.
- Validates that the number is an integer in `Float` range.
- Returns a `BigNumber` instance of type `Float`.

The `toDouble` cast function will do the following:
- Validates that the value is a numeric type.
- Validates that the number is an integer in `Double` range.
- Returns a `BigNumber` instance of type `Double`.

## UUIDs

To pass a `Uuid` to a function, use the `toUuid` cast function.
To create a `Uuid` object, use the `createUuid` function.
